en: in minute detail; every little thing

examples.ko: 엄마가 어제 있었던 일을 미주알고주알 물어보셨어요.
examples.en: Mom asked about everything that happened yesterday in detail.

examples.ko: 친구는 데이트 이야기를 미주알고주알 다 말해 줬어요.
examples.en: My friend told me every detail of her date.
Don't nitpick over every detail, just let it go.
Grandmother went on about every bit of neighborhood gossip.

examples.ko: 아이가 학교에서 있었던 일을 미주알고주알 이야기해요.
examples.en: The child tells me everything that happened at school.
The interviewer pried into everything, even my family.

explain: 사소한 것까지 하나하나 캐묻거나 낱낱이 말할 때 써요. '캐묻다', '따지다', '말하다' 같은 동사와 자주 같이 나와요. 귀찮거나 지나치다는 느낌이 들 때가 많아요.

phrases.en: The police questioned me about every little detail.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사소한 것까지 끝까지 물어서 귀찮은 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Suggests being asked about even tiny things, which feels bothersome.

phrases.example: 그는 회사에서 있었던 일을 미주알고주알 말해요.
phrases.en: He tells me every little thing that happened at work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 일까지 빠짐없이 다 말한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means telling everything, down to the smallest matters.

phrases.example: 영수증을 보며 미주알고주알 따지는 손님 때문에 힘들었어요.
phrases.en: It was tough dealing with a customer who nitpicked every line of the receipt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 잘못까지 하나하나 따질 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone argues over every small fault.

explain_en: Use it when asking about or telling every small detail one by one. It often pairs with verbs like '캐묻다' (pry), '따지다' (nitpick) and '말하다' (tell). It often feels annoying or excessive.

examples.en: He disguised himself to avoid the police.
The kids dressed up as witches at the party.
Even if you disguise yourself, I know you from your voice.
The scene where the actor disguises himself as a grandmother was funny.
They say a celebrity came to the market in disguise.
She was disguised, so nobody recognized her.

explain: '변장하다'는 정체를 숨기거나 다른 사람처럼 보이려고 옷차림과 얼굴을 바꾸는 거예요. 배우가 역할에 맞게 꾸미는 건 '분장'이라고 해요. '변장'은 누군가를 속이거나 알아보지 못하게 하려는 목적이 있을 때 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: He went into the party while still in disguise.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ 채로'를 붙여 변장한 상태가 계속될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -ㄴ 채로 means staying in the disguised state.

phrases.example: 변장한 모습이 너무 달라서 못 알아봤어요.
phrases.en: He looked so different in disguise that I didn't recognize him.
phrases.nuance_ko: 변장한 상태의 겉모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about how someone looks when disguised.

phrases.en: I heard the thief ran away in disguise.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정체를 숨기려는 목적과 잘 이어지는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs well with the purpose of hiding one's identity.

explain_en: 변장하다 means changing your clothes and face to hide who you are or pass as someone else. When an actor is made up for a role, the word is 분장. 변장 fits best when the aim is to fool people or avoid being recognized.

en: to move out; to set up a household

examples.en: I moved out of my parents' home when I got married.
My younger sibling also plans to move out soon.

examples.ko: 아들이 직장 때문에 분가해서 따로 살아요.
examples.en: My son moved out because of his job and lives separately.
My uncle moved out a long time ago.
When would be a good time to move out?

examples.ko: 우리 부부는 아이가 태어나기 전에 분가해요.
examples.en: My spouse and I are moving out before the baby is born.

explain: 주로 결혼한 자녀가 부모님 집에서 나와 따로 사는 경우에 써서, 혼자 사는 '자취하다'와는 느낌이 달라요. 높이면 '분가하셨어요'라고 하고, 반대말은 '합가하다'예요. 요즘 대화에서는 '독립하다'도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: We moved out and live in a small house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나온 뒤 따로 사는 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe living separately after moving out.
phrases.en_equiv: to live separately after moving out

phrases.en: The eldest son moved out last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람이나 다른 사람의 가족을 높여 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to speak respectfully about an elder or someone else's family.

phrases.en: I want to move out on my own next year too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결혼하지 않아도 쓸 수 있어서 '분가하다'보다 더 넓게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can be used even without marriage, so broader than '분가하다'.

explain_en: Leaving family home to live independently, often after marriage. It is mostly used when a married child leaves the parents' home to live separately, which feels different from '자취하다' (living alone). The honorific form is '분가하셨어요', and the opposite is '합가하다'. In conversation today '독립하다' is also very common.

t90.ax: My uncle moved out a long time ago.

en: to sponge off; to mooch off; to fawn on

examples.ko: 그는 친구 집에 빌붙어 몇 달째 살고 있어요.
examples.en: He has been mooching off his friend's place for months now.

examples.ko: 남에게 빌붙지 말고 스스로 일해서 살아요.
examples.en: Don't sponge off others; work and live on your own.

examples.ko: 부잣집에 빌붙어서 편하게 지내려는 사람이 있어요.
examples.en: There are people who try to live comfortably by clinging to a rich family.
My younger brother, who used to mooch off his older brother, finally got a job.

examples.ko: 권력자에게 빌붙는 사람들을 저는 좋아하지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't like people who suck up to those in power.
How long are you going to keep living off your parents?

explain: '얹혀살다'는 남의 집에서 신세 지며 사는 것 자체를 말하는 반면, '빌붙다'는 이익을 챙기려고 달라붙는 나쁜 느낌이 더 강해요. 돈이나 힘 있는 사람에게 기대어 사는 사람에게 쓰기 때문에, 앞에 있는 사람에게 말하면 모욕이 될 수 있어요.

phrases.en: He mooches off his older brother, living in his house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남에게 기대어 사는 것을 안 좋게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to speak badly about living off someone.

phrases.en: Don't mooch off others.
phrases.nuance_ko: 충고할 때 쓰지만 듣는 사람 기분이 나쁠 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as advice, but it can offend the listener.

phrases.en: I'm staying at a friend's place for a while.
phrases.nuance_ko: '빌붙다'보다 나쁜 느낌이 약하고 신세 지는 상황만 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Less negative than 빌붙다; it only describes being a guest.

explain_en: Negative, flattering a powerful person for profit. '얹혀살다' simply describes living at someone else's expense, while '빌붙다' carries a stronger negative sense of clinging on to gain benefits. It is used for people who lean on those with money or power, so saying it to someone's face can be insulting.

t90.ax: I don't like people who suck up to those in power.

en: to be bereaved of; to be separated from someone by death

examples.en: My grandmother lost my grandfather a long time ago.

examples.ko: 젊은 나이에 남편과 사별해서 혼자 아이를 키웠어요.
examples.en: She lost her husband at a young age and raised the child alone.

examples.ko: 아내와 사별한 뒤 그분은 말수가 줄었어요.
examples.en: After losing his wife, that person spoke less.
When you lose your spouse, it is hard to pull yourself together.
Losing a family member is hard for anyone.
I heard the news that my friend lost their mother.

explain: '헤어지다'와 달리 죽음으로 이별했다는 뜻이 이 말에 들어 있어요. 주로 남편이나 아내에게 쓰고, 'A와 사별하다'처럼 '와/과'를 붙여요. 부모는 '여의다'를 더 자주 써요. 이혼은 '이혼하다'라고 해서 사별과 달라요.

phrases.en: After losing her husband, she went back to her hometown.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사별 이후의 삶을 이야기할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to talk about life after a spouse's death.

phrases.example: 배우자와 사별한 분들을 위한 모임이 있어요.
phrases.en: There is a gathering for people who have lost a spouse.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사별하다가 주로 부부 사이에 쓰인다는 점을 보여 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows that this word is mainly used between spouses.

phrases.example: 사별의 아픔을 이겨 내기가 쉽지 않아요.
phrases.en: It is not easy to get over the pain of bereavement.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 사별에 감정을 나타내는 말을 붙인 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun form paired with a word for emotion.

explain_en: Unlike '헤어지다' (to part), this word itself carries the meaning that the parting was through death. It is mostly used for a husband or wife, in the pattern 'A와 사별하다'. For parents, '여의다' is more common. Divorce is '이혼하다', a different thing.

examples.ko: 생면부지의 사람이 길에서 제 짐을 들어 줬어요.
examples.en: A complete stranger helped carry my bags on the street.
I started living alone in a place where I knew no one.

examples.ko: 생면부지였던 두 사람이 이제는 가장 친한 친구예요.
examples.en: The two who were once total strangers are now the closest of friends.
I received help from a total stranger and tears came to my eyes.
I felt shy about asking a person I'd never met for directions.

examples.ko: 생면부지라서 처음엔 서로 말도 못 걸었어요.
examples.en: We were complete strangers, so at first we couldn't even speak to each other.

explain: 한 번도 만난 적 없는 사람뿐 아니라 '생면부지의 땅'처럼 처음 가 보는 곳에도 써요. '모르는 사람'보다 강조하는 느낌이 있고, 말보다는 글에서 더 잘 어울려요.

phrases.example: 생면부지의 사람이 저에게 길을 알려 줬어요.
phrases.en: A complete stranger showed me the way.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의'와 함께 써서 전혀 모르는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '의', it refers to someone you don't know at all.

phrases.example: 저는 생면부지의 땅에서 새 삶을 시작했어요.
phrases.en: I started a new life in a land I had never known.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람뿐 아니라 처음 가 보는 곳에도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Works for places you've never been, not just people.

explain_en: It is used not only for someone you have never met but also for a place you've never been, as in '생면부지의 땅'. It is stronger than '모르는 사람' (someone I don't know) and suits writing better than casual speech.

en: to cheer on; to support enthusiastically; to back

examples.ko: 많은 분들이 우리 팀을 성원해 주셨어요.
examples.en: Many people cheered on our team.

examples.ko: 끝까지 성원해 주신 팬 여러분께 감사드려요.
examples.en: Thank you to the fans who supported us to the end.
The audience cheering for the athlete was moving.
I will keep supporting you as always.

examples.ko: 응원단이 큰 소리로 성원하자 선수들이 힘을 냈어요.
examples.en: When the cheering squad backed them loudly, the players found new energy.
Citizens eagerly backed the national team.

explain: '응원하다'보다 격식 있고 글이나 인사말에서 많이 써요. 보통 '성원해 주셔서 감사합니다'처럼 도와준 사람에게 고마움을 말할 때 자주 나와요. 가까운 사이의 일상 대화에서는 '응원해'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Please give our team a lot of support.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부탁하는 인사말로 쓰며 공손하고 격식 있는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite, formal way to ask people for their support.

phrases.en: We thank you all for your support.
phrases.nuance_ko: 응원해 준 사람에게 고마움을 전하는 대표적인 인사말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical expression for thanking people who have cheered you on.

phrases.en: I cheered for my friend's game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 같지만 일상 대화에서 더 편하게 써요. '성원하다'는 글이나 인사말에 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning but more casual and common in daily talk, while 성원하다 suits writing and greetings.

explain_en: Formal, warm support, often thanks to fans (성원해 주세요) More formal than '응원하다' and common in writing and greetings. You mostly hear it when thanking supporters, as in '성원해 주셔서 감사합니다'. In casual talk between close people, Koreans just say '응원해'.

t90.ax: Many people cheered on our team.

examples.en: The kids are gathered together talking in whispers.

examples.ko: 뒤에서 누가 수군수군 얘기하는 소리가 들려요.
examples.en: I can hear someone whispering behind me.

examples.ko: 두 사람이 수군수군 비밀 이야기를 나눠요.
examples.en: The two of them share secrets in whispers.
In the library, even whispers can be heard by everyone.
My friends were whispering and laughing next to me.

examples.ko: 수군수군 말하지 말고 크게 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Please don't whisper, speak up.

explain: '속닥속닥'처럼 작은 소리로 말하는 모양을 나타내는데, 여러 사람이 남 이야기를 하는 느낌이 있어요. 동사로는 '수군대다'를 쓰는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: Kids are whispering at the back of the classroom.
phrases.nuance_ko: '하다'를 붙여 동사처럼 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 하다 turns it into a verb.

phrases.en: The two of them are chatting in whispers.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수군수군'보다 비밀 이야기 같은 느낌이 더 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels more like sharing secrets than 수군수군.

phrases.en: My friends laughed while whispering.
phrases.nuance_ko: '말하다'와 함께 쓰면 낮은 소리로 이야기하는 모습이 잘 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 말하다, it shows speaking in low voices.

explain_en: Murmuring in a group, often gossip behind others' backs. Like '속닥속닥', it describes talking in low voices, but it often suggests several people talking about someone else. The matching verb is '수군대다'.

en: to talk in whispers; to talk low

examples.en: The villagers whispered to each other after hearing the rumor.
You shouldn't whisper during a meeting.
The two whispered something and then suddenly laughed.
I heard whispering in the hallway.

examples.ko: 내 앞에서 쑥덕거리지 말고 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Don't whisper in front of me; just tell me.

examples.ko: 이웃들이 새로 이사 온 집을 두고 쑥덕거려요.
examples.en: The neighbors are whispering about the family that just moved in.

explain: 소문이나 남의 흉을 몰래 주고받는 장면에 써서 부정적인 느낌이 강해요. 그냥 조용히 말하는 것은 '속삭이다'라고 해요. '쑤군거리다'와 바꿔 써도 돼요.

phrases.en: They are whispering at the back of the classroom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몰래 낮게 말하는 모양을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows the manner of whispering secretly.

phrases.en: People are whispering behind my back.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쑥덕거리다'와 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can be swapped with 쑥덕거리다.

phrases.en: You shouldn't badmouth others.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남의 단점을 몰래 말한다는 점에서 이어져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Links through talking about others' faults.

explain_en: Stronger variant of (숙덕거리다); often gossiping or plotting behind someone's back (뒤에서 쑥덕거리다). It is used for secretly trading rumors or gossip about others, so it feels negative. Simply speaking quietly is '속삭이다'. You can swap it with '쑤군거리다'.

t90.ax: I heard whispering in the hallway.

en: to be small but tough and spirited

examples.en: That child is small but tough.
The little girl answered in a firm, spirited voice.
She may be short, but she works with grit.
That player fought hard and won the ball.
My younger brother stood up fiercely to his older brother.

examples.ko: 암팡진 성격 덕분에 어려움을 이겨 냈어요.
examples.en: Thanks to her gutsy personality, she overcame the hardship.

explain: 몸집은 작은데 야무지고 당찬 모습에 써요. '야무지다'와 비슷하지만 작은 몸에 비해 힘차다는 느낌이 더 있어요. '암팡지게 달려들다', '암팡진 목소리'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 작은 강아지가 큰 개에게 암팡지게 달려들었어요.
phrases.en: The little puppy lunged fiercely at the big dog.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 몸으로 힘차게 맞서는 모습을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly used for a small one boldly taking on something bigger.

phrases.example: 그 아이는 어른 앞에서도 암팡지게 말해요.
phrases.en: That child speaks boldly even in front of adults.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말투가 당차고 거침없다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Suggests a spunky, unhesitating way of speaking.

phrases.en: My younger sibling is young but really sharp and capable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 뜻이지만 '암팡지다'처럼 작은 몸에 비해 힘차다는 느낌은 덜해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar, but lacks the 'tough for such a small body' feel of 'amphangjida'.

explain_en: It is used for someone small in build but firm, capable and spirited. It is similar to '야무지다' but has more of a feeling of being strong for one's small size. Typical uses are '암팡지게 달려들다' and '암팡진 목소리'.

examples.ko: 얼간이 같은 실수를 해서 너무 부끄러워요.
examples.en: I made such a stupid mistake and I'm so embarrassed.

examples.ko: 그 얼간이가 비밀번호를 친구한테 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: That fool told his friend the password.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 얼간이는 아니지만 좀 느려요.
examples.en: He's not an idiot, but he's a bit slow.
Only I didn't know anything, like a fool.

examples.ko: 그렇게 쉬운 걸 틀리다니 제가 얼간이였어요.
examples.en: I got something that easy wrong. I was such an idiot.

examples.ko: 친구에게 얼간이라고 하면 싸울 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you call a friend an idiot, you might end up fighting.

explain: 모자라고 어리숙한 사람을 낮잡아 부르는 말이라, 상대에게 직접 쓰면 모욕이 될 수 있어요. 친한 사이의 농담이나 자기 자신을 탓할 때 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 비슷한 말로 '바보', '멍청이'가 있어요.

phrases.en: I'm a fool who forgot the appointment again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하지만 '얼간이'보다 덜 거칠고 더 흔히 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning but milder and more common than 얼간이.

phrases.example: 문을 잠그지 않고 나온 제가 멍청이 같아요.
phrases.en: I feel like an idiot for leaving without locking the door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 낮춰 부르는 말이라 자기 자신에게 쓰는 편이 안전해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A harsher put-down, so it is safer to use about yourself.

phrases.example: 시험 날짜를 잊다니 제가 얼간이처럼 굴었어요.
phrases.en: I acted like a fool by forgetting the exam date.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어리숙하게 행동했다고 스스로를 탓할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to blame yourself for acting foolishly.

explain_en: It looks down on someone who is foolish or easily fooled, so saying it directly to a person can be insulting. It is often used as a joke between close friends or to blame oneself. Similar words are '바보' and '멍청이'.

t90.ax: That fool told his friend the password.

examples.en: The director of this drama is a famous filmmaker.
The director explained the scene to the actors.
A stage director is responsible for the whole stage.
The director and the actor talked for a long time.
It was hard to understand the director's intention.
The director received an award at the ceremony.

explain: 영화는 '감독'이라고 부르고, 연극이나 방송, 공연은 '연출자'나 '연출가'라는 말을 많이 써요. 방송에서는 PD가 연출자 역할을 하는 때가 많아요. '연출'은 장면을 짜고 배우를 이끄는 일을 가리켜요.

phrases.example: 그 연출가는 연극을 이십 년 넘게 만들었어요.
phrases.en: That director has been making plays for over twenty years.
phrases.nuance_ko: '연출자'와 거의 같고, 연극이나 공연에서 조금 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same as 'yeonchulja', a bit more common for plays and performances.

phrases.en: A famous director directed this drama.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장면을 짜고 배우를 이끄는 일을 하는 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb for staging scenes and guiding actors.

phrases.en: The director of this movie is a newcomer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영화에서는 '연출자'보다 '감독'이라고 부르는 경우가 더 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: For films, people more often say 'gamdok' than 'yeonchulja'.

explain_en: For movies the usual word is 감독, while for plays, broadcasts and performances 연출자 or 연출가 is common. In broadcasting, a PD often plays the role of the 연출자. 연출 is the work of arranging the scenes and guiding the actors.

examples.en: The family gathers cozily and eats dinner.
The old couple chats warmly together.

examples.ko: 친구들과 오순도순 사는 게 제 꿈이에요.
examples.en: My dream is to live peacefully with my friends.
The brothers get along so well, which is nice to see.
The neighbors live sharing warm feelings with each other.
Let's get along nicely.

explain: 사이좋게 정답게 모여 지내거나 이야기하는 모습에 써요. 주로 가족, 이웃, 친구처럼 가까운 사람들에게 쓰고, 보통 '지내다, 살다, 이야기하다'와 함께 나와요.

phrases.en: The neighbors get along warmly with each other.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사이좋게 함께 생활한다는 뜻으로 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common use, meaning living together on good terms.

phrases.en: The brothers live together in harmony.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가족이나 한 집에서 사는 사람들에게 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits family members or people sharing a home.

phrases.en: I chatted cozily with my grandmother.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정답게 이야기를 나누는 장면에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For a warm, friendly conversation.

explain_en: It describes people getting along warmly, whether living together or talking. It is mostly used for close people like family, neighbors and friends, and usually goes with '지내다', '살다' and '이야기하다'.

examples.en: They say the famous writer passed away last night.
He passed away quietly in the hospital.
I wrote down the date he passed away in the book.
Before passing away, he left a letter for his family.

examples.ko: 삼 년 전에 운명한 시인의 시를 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read a poem by a poet who passed away three years ago.
Everyone was shocked at the news that he had passed away.

explain: '죽다'보다 아주 격식 있는 말이에요. 주로 신문 기사나 장례식 같은 자리에서 써요. 높일 때는 '돌아가시다'가 훨씬 더 일반적이니 일상에서는 '돌아가시다'를 쓰세요. 소리가 같은 '운명'(타고난 앞날)과 헷갈리지 마세요.

phrases.en: I heard the news that the writer passed away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사망 소식을 격식 있게 전할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to convey news of a death in a formal way.

phrases.en: I paid my respects to the family of the person who passed away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돌아가신 분을 높여서 부를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to respectfully refer to the person who has died.

phrases.en: My grandfather passed away last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '운명하다'보다 일상에서 훨씬 많이 쓰는 높임말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This honorific is used far more often in daily life than '운명하다'.

explain_en: Literary/formal; stresses the moment of death, used in reports. This is a very formal word for dying, mainly in newspaper articles and funeral settings. In daily life, '돌아가시다' is far more common when showing respect, so use that. Do not confuse it with the same-sounding '운명' (fate).

dis.h: literary: breathe one's last, moment of death
gh: everyday polite word for elders dying
written word for famous figures dying

p.n: 돌아가시다 is the everyday polite way; 운명하다 sounds literary.

t90.ax: He passed away quietly in the hospital.
